messages:
sophie: FYI ACMEProd is seeing persistent 429s during a 2k->8k RPS burst on their dedicated pool. They say the autoscaler spins up new nodes but requests still queue. stack traces show "attach handshake timeout" and lots of short-lived retries. Putting logs + repro below.

samir: Can you paste the earliest attach/scale logs and the burst pattern? Also which min_replicas / headroom are they on?

sophie: min_replicas=1, target_rps=150, headroom=2. Burst pattern: ramp 2k -> 8k over 45s, sustained 90s, then drop. Customer timeline: spikes start at 14:02:10, API 429s at 14:02:22. They reported explicit errors: "attach request timed out after 12s" from control-plane. Quick repro (staging):

```bash
# synthetic burst: 200 clients, 40 qps each ~8k total
wrk -t200 -c200 -d90s -R8000 http://redwood-dedicated.example/v1/generate
```

and a little tail of the control-plane event stream captured: 

```
[14:02:12] scale-controller: requested new node pool=dedicated-acme-42 count=3
[14:02:18] node-manager: node created id=i-0ab123 init=ok
[14:02:20] attach-service: attach_req id=abc123 -> pending handshake
[14:02:22] attach-service: attach_req id=abc123 -> handshake timeout after 12s
[14:02:22] autoscaler: scale not observed, backoff schedule applied
[14:02:23] api-gateway: 429 backlog=180
```

liam: Can you check model runtime init logs on the new nodes? If the runtime blocks on model shard pull, attach will appear timed out even though instance exists. Also did registry show any 429s?

sophie: I pulled a few node logs, here's the startup tail: 

```
[init] pulling model shard url=https://models.internal/acme-v2/part-3
[init] fetch failed 429 TooManyRequests (x-amz-rate-limited)
[init] retrying backoff 2s
[init] model init blocked, runtime state=unready
```

jess: We also saw a token rotation event in the customer account around 14:01:55 (short-lived STS failures). It aligns with the window where attach requests started failing. Could be two independent amplifiers: registry rate-limit + ephemeral auth errors.

samir: Hypothesis: autoscaler creates node quickly but the node cannot finish runtime init because of model registry throttling (and occasional STS denies). The attach handshake times out and autoscaler treats the scale as failed so it stops attempting more capacity (due to our conservative backoff/min_replicas). That leaves live traffic queued on the single warm node.

infra-bot: Recent events summary attached: 
```
E 14:01:55 auth: sts assume-role failed status=403 request=rot_xxx
W 14:02:17 registry: pull 429 for model acme-v2 part-3 client=service-model-fetcher
E 14:02:22 attach: handshake timeout id=abc123
```

liam: Immediate mitigation options: (1) bump min_replicas to 3 for this customer while we diagnose, (2) increase attach handshake timeout, (3) add retryable warm-pool prefetch for model shards, (4) route fallback to hosted path for a subset of traffic. Which can we authorize quickly?

sophie: Customer approved temp min_replicas bump if we own the cost. They'll accept reroute to hosted for critical endpoints for 30m.

samir: Longer term fixes: make autoscaler observe node readiness from runtime health endpoint (not just node creation), improve model-pull backoff jitter, surface registry 429s to autoscaler so it can avoid treating creation as failed, and add a pre-warm step that prefetches hot model shards into warm pool nodes. I'll create an engineering ticket.

jess: For triage owners: eng-platform to follow up on autoscaler readiness signal (samir), infra to look at registry rate limits + mitigation (liam), customer success to coordinate billing/cost (sophie).

sophie: Repro notes we left for staging: 
1) create dedicated pool with min_replicas=1, headroom=2, attach_timeout=12s
2) seed registry with 4GB model split into multiple shards with enforced 429 throttling (nginx limit)
3) run wrk burst script above
4) verify attach timeouts and autoscaler backoff behavior

samir: I'll add a minimal repro script and test tomorrow in staging. For now I pushed the temporary min_replicas bump and a 5-minute route fallback to hosted. Monitoring: watch api 429s and attach timeout counts. :eyes:

sophie: Customer on-call confirmed traffic dropped to <5% 429s after fallback. They're happy for a staged fix plan. :thumbsup:

#action: ENG-PLATFORM-789 create readiness-observed-autoscale ticket (samir)
#action: INFRA-456 investigate registry rate-limit & token rotation race (liam)
#action: CS-321 coordinate temporary bill approval for min_replicas bump (sophie)
